newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish insurer PZU's listing seen in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Polish insurer PZU's listing seen in 1997.

text.p: Poland's biggest insurer, state -owned Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU), will offer its shares to domestic investors at the turn of the year and plans Warsaw listing in 1997, a finance ministry official said.

"The first step of the privatisation will be a new share issue directed to domestic institutions, and the next will be a public offering in mid-1997 or in the second half of 1997," Anatol Adamski, the head of the ministry's insurance department, told Reuters.
He said it was too early to give any details on the issues. @
He told Reuters the privatisation plan did not envisage seeking strategic investors for the company, which had a 60-percent share of the Polish non-life market.
Earlier PZU has said it wanted to start its privatisation in late 1996 with a new share issue for Polish investors which would give them a 24-percent stake.
Under the original plan this issue would be followed later by a share offer for the insurer's employees and a later offering for foreign financial institutions. @
Adamski said the privatisation of PZU would be combined with a gradual sell-off of its life subsidiary PZU Zycie SA, a , but he said the life firm's privatisation strategy would be worked out later.
PZU had a net profit of 105.2 million zlotys on gross premiums of 2.2 billion zlotys in 1995. It netted 52 million zlotys in the first half of 1996.

PZU Zycie netted 58.1 million zlotys on gross premiums of 1.6 billion zlotys in 1995 and had a net profit of 55.4 million zlotys in the first half of 1996. PZU Zycie has has an 87-percent share of the Polish life-insurance market.
